transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
The Tennessee woman who survived a failed execution is now awake.
Katherine Sweeney at member station WPLN gives us the latest.
Christa Pike has been hospitalized since Wednesday.
That's when Tennessee tried and failed to put her to death for her role in the 1995
killing of Colleen Slimmer.
The prison administered two doses of lethal drugs, but she ultimately left in an ambulance.
Her attorneys announced Tuesday afternoon she was not only conscious, but speaking.
They said she was handcuffed to her bed, even though her arms are covered in burns and blisters.
They attribute those injuries to bad IV placement during her attempted execution, and say it's
likely the Pinto Barbatol intended to kill her flowed into her flesh instead of into
her bloodstream.
For NPR News, I'm Katherine Sweeney in Nashville.
Threats of Iranian inspired attacks led the U.S. to move all of its bombers from a military
base in the United Kingdom.
And PR's Tom Bowman reports modern drone warfare is prompting officials to consider boosting
security at bases around the world or leave.
It's a serious problem, as we've already seen at U.S. bases around the Middle East.
These planes are not in hardened shelters, but out in the open.
I had coffee with a NATO military officer who was talking about this very topic just this
week.
You could take a cheap drone, put a grenade on it, and do at least some damage to a B-1
bomber, a $317 million aircraft.
NPR's Tom Bowman reporting Skydance-owned Paramount has closed its $81 billion takeover
of Warner Bros. Discovery.
The new Hollywood giant will be known simply as Skydance.
The merger concentrates power in an industry already run by just a handful of major players.
HBO Max and networks such as CNN now find themselves under the same roof as Paramount
Plus and CBS.
German authorities have arrested two people, including the country's former spy chief
in connection with suspected espionage.
Esme Nicholson reports prosecutors have not yet commented on whether the men were spying
for a foreign actor.
Germany's federal prosecutor's office says Auguste Haning will be brought before a federal
judge on charges that include treasonous espionage and attempted treason.
Haning, now 80, served as the head of Germany's foreign intelligence agency known as the BND
between 1998 and 2005.
Officers have also arrested a current intelligence officer named only as Manfred D. for allegedly
aiding and abetting attempted treason and treasonous espionage.
The aide is suspected of providing the intelligence agency's former chief with thousands of classified
documents in exchange for money.
Haning then allegedly used this information for his private consultancy work.
For NPR News, I'm Esme Nicholson in Berlin.
A tropical rainstorm has formed in the Gulf of Mexico and could make landfall this weekend
as a strong tropical storm somewhere near Mobile Bay.
The next name on the list of Atlantic storms is Isaias.
This is NPR News from Washington.
Student loan borrowers now have until the end of 2026 to enroll in autopay and have
their interest rate reduced by 1 percent.
The original deadline was September 30th, but the Department of Education extended it
to give borrowers more time to enroll.
The rate reduction will last through June 2028.
Around 9 million Americans are in default on their federal student loans.
A group of leftist organizers in the U.S. are launching a "defendance union" to help
people who are targets of National Security Presidential Memorandum 7, or NSPM 7, and
NPR's Odette Yousef reports.
Last year, President Trump issued NSPM 7 associating certain ideologies such as anti-fascism, anti-capitalism,
and anti-Christianity with threats to national security.
Organizers of the NSPM 7 defendants union say their goal is to bring targets of these
cases together to publicly resist what they call politicized prosecutions.
Clara spoke to NPR on condition of using only her first name due to fear of retaliation by
the federal government.
The idea of these federal cases is to scare people and movements into breaking apart.
Last month, FBI Director Kash Patel said his agency has overseen arrests of more than 200
people pursuant to the NSPM 7 directive.
Odette Yousef, NPR News.
Stanley Kubrick's personal archive is up for auction.
The collection features iconic items from his films.
Highlights include the axe wielded by Jack Nicholson in "The Shining" and the prop
infant from 2001 "A Space Odyssey."
This is NPR News from Washington.

topics.text: Tennessee woman Christa Pike conscious and speaking after failed execution Wednesday
U.S. moves all bombers from UK military base due to Iranian-inspired attack threats
Skydance completes $81 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery, creating new Hollywood giant
Germany arrests former spy chief Auguste Haning on espionage and treason charges
Tropical rainstorm forms in Gulf of Mexico, could reach Mobile Bay this weekend
Student loan borrowers get extended deadline until end of 2026 for autopay enrollment
Leftist organizers launch union to defend people targeted under Trump's NSPM 7 directive
Stanley Kubrick personal archive featuring iconic film items going up for auction
